summary: Organ-specific growth trajectories are published piecemeal, as the assessors expected: the only repository deposit found that measures part-by-part growth through ontogeny is a single trilobite species (Dryad 10.5061/dryad.6069g, CC0), and the pig craniofacial dataset (10.5061/dryad.tdz08kqb1) compares two breeds postnatally. IMPC gives adult organ weights and body-weight curves across thousands of mouse genotypes, BIA holds chick/zebrafish whole-organism time-lapse from which organ sizes could be segmented, Add-my-Pet is whole-body only, BioNumbers has isolated values, and the e-Mouse Atlas was unreachable.
next_step: Define the test on a tractable system with existing series (pig breeds 10.5061/dryad.tdz08kqb1 for cranial parts; IMPC organ weights vs body weight across genotypes), or compile organ-mass-by-age tables for two related mammals from the literature; then pre-register how much adult shape difference the local-rate differences predict.
obstacles_confirmed: Organ-specific growth rates are published piecemeal: no multi-species organ-trajectory dataset in Dryad, DataCite or Zenodo.
Comparable trajectories across taxa are sparse: the one ontogenetic part-growth deposit found is a single fossil species.
e-Mouse Atlas unreachable in three attempts.
